name: How Big a Threat?
summary: Terenthis asks scouts in Auberdine to learn whether furbolg corruption has reached Darkshore. After madness takes hold among furbolgs in Teldrassil, the night elf druid sends them to inspect mainland settlements across the sea.

sections.title: Shadows Across the Sea
sections.body: Night elves across northern Kalimdor have long lived peacefully with the furbolg tribes. Since the Third War, strange corruption has unhinged furbolg minds in Teldrassil. They have kidnapped and attacked their former allies. Terenthis, a druid stationed in Auberdine, fears the affliction has spread beyond the World Tree to the mainland tribes along Darkshore’s coast.

sections.title: A Gathering Storm
sections.body: A furbolg camp near the ruins of Ameth'Aran shows signs of the same corruption found in northern Teldrassil. The furbolgs there act erratically and attack without cause. Because the camp lies close to Auberdine, its hostile inhabitants now threaten the Alliance settlement.

aliases: who gives how big a threat
faq.answer: Terenthis is a night elf druid stationed in Auberdine. Accounts of maddened furbolgs attacking and capturing night elves across Teldrassil have led him to watch for threats throughout Darkshore.

faq.q: Why are the furbolgs in Darkshore turning hostile?
faq.answer: Terenthis has seen hints of corruption in Darkshore and suspects the furbolgs may be affected, as some on Teldrassil were. He asks for their camps to be investigated because he has not yet established widespread signs.

faq.q: Where is the corrupt furbolg camp located?
faq.answer: The encampment lies inland in central Darkshore, just north of the ancient highborne ruins of Ameth'Aran and southeast of Auberdine.

faq.q: How does this relate to events on Teldrassil?
faq.answer: In Teldrassil, corrupted furbolgs kidnapped and injured night elf sentinels and civilians. Terenthis points to those recent rescues as he seeks to learn whether mainland Darkshore faces the same crisis.

faq.q: What happens after reporting back to Terenthis?
aliases: what follows how big a threat
faq.answer: Tell Terenthis in Auberdine if you find signs of corruption. His response comes when you return.

faq.q: Why are night elves so concerned about furbolg camps near Auberdine?
faq.answer: Auberdine is the Alliance's main port and supply route on the mainland. Hostile, deeply corrupted tribes close to town could threaten trade roads, scouts and the settlement itself.

angles.text: As a kaldorei, you see ancient allies like the furbolgs fall to irrational darkness soon after the Third War. Their corruption threatens sacred lands as well as old bonds.
As a druid, you know furbolgs share deep bonds with nature and ancient wilderness spirits. Their sudden corruption is a grave concern for those who heal Kalimdor's balance.
As an Alliance member, you depend on Auberdine as the Alliance's main gateway to mainland northern Kalimdor. Its safety matters to the region's security and supply routes.
